exposure: Balloon tamponade and bilateral uterine artery ligation
Bilateral uterine artery ligation and cervical inversion
cohort: 125 patients with morbidly adherent placenta who underwent elective cesarean section at 35-38 weeks gestation
finding: Bilateral uterine artery ligation combined with cervical inversion was more effective than balloon tamponade with or without bilateral uterine artery ligation for controlling hemorrhage from morbidly adherent placenta, resulting in less blood loss, lower blood transfusion rates, shorter hospital stays, and reduced complications.
